questions.stem: An application's traffic follows a daily pattern that shifts slowly over the months, and new instances need about 10 minutes before they can serve traffic. The team created a predictive scaling policy two weeks ago, and the forecasts look accurate, but the Auto Scaling group still does not add capacity before the morning peak. The team wants capacity to be ready ahead of the peak without maintaining fixed schedules. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Change the policy from forecast only to forecast and scale, and set pre-launch instances to about 10 minutes.
Keep the policy in forecast only mode, and wait for it to learn more of the pattern.
Replace the policy with recurring scheduled actions that use cron expressions for the morning peak.
Delete the policy and create it again so that it starts scaling from the first day.

questions.stem: A company exposes a TCP-based service to a partner. The partner's firewall allows outbound traffic only to a fixed list of IP addresses, one per Availability Zone that the company uses. Each TCP connection must stay with a single backend target for its lifetime. The company does not need any HTTP-level routing. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?

choices.text: A Network Load Balancer with one Elastic IP address associated with the network interface in each enabled Availability Zone.
An Application Load Balancer with listener rules that route requests by path to a target group.
A Network Load Balancer whose DNS name the partner adds to its firewall instead of IP addresses.
One Amazon EC2 instance with an Elastic IP address that forwards connections to the backend targets.

questions.stem: A product catalog service reads from Amazon ElastiCache in front of a database. After products are updated in the database, users sometimes see old prices from the cache. The company wants cached data to stay current after writes, wants new cache nodes added during scale-out to fill in missing data, and wants to avoid filling the cache with data that is never read. Which actions should the company take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Update the cache every time the application writes to the database (write-through).
Also load data into the cache on a cache miss (lazy loading), and set a TTL on cached items.
Keep only lazy loading, because it never returns stale data.
Use write-through without any TTL so that every written item stays in the cache permanently.
Disable the cache whenever a node fails, because node failures are fatal with lazy loading.
